name: US Federal Statutory Policy Pack
description: Statutory rules grounded in federal law: ROSCA, FTC Negative Option Rule, Federal Arbitration Act, and FTC Act Section 5.

rules.title: Negative Option Automatic Renewal

statute.title: Restore Online Shoppers Confidence Act & FTC Negative Option Rule
statute.plainExplanation: Federal ROSCA and FTC Negative Option regulations require clear, conspicuous disclosure of recurring terms and explicit affirmative consumer consent prior to initial billing.

rules.explanation: The agreement binds you to automated recurring charges that renew indefinitely until you affirmatively navigate their cancellation procedure.
rules.recommendation: Verify that clear, upfront billing disclosures and an online cancellation button are present before submitting payment.

rules.title: Asymmetrical Cancellation Dark Pattern (Call/Mail-Only)

statute.title: FTC Click-to-Cancel Mandate & Deceptive Practices Rule
statute.plainExplanation: If you subscribed online, FTC enforcement and Click-to-Cancel rules require that you must be allowed to cancel online through the same medium without having to call or mail.

rules.explanation: The agreement forces you to call customer support or mail physical letters to cancel a subscription initiated online.
rules.recommendation: Do not agree unless an immediate online cancellation button is available in your account dashboard.

rules.title: Mandatory Binding Arbitration & Jury Waiver

statute.code: 9 U.S.C. § 2 (FAA Enforcement) / U.S. Const. amend. VII
statute.title: Federal Arbitration Act & 7th Amendment Jury Right
statute.plainExplanation: Enforceable under the Federal Arbitration Act (9 U.S.C. § 2). While lawful, it compels consumers to resolve disputes in private confidential forums instead of public courtrooms.

rules.explanation: Lawful under federal law, but you surrender your constitutional right to a jury trial and access to a public court of law if the company harms you.
rules.recommendation: Check whether the agreement includes a 30-day opt-out window to reject arbitration while maintaining your account.

rules.title: Class Action & Collective Lawsuit Waiver

statute.code: Fed. R. Civ. P. 23 / AT&T Mobility LLC v. Concepcion
statute.title: Class Action Ban & Representative Action Waiver
statute.plainExplanation: Prevents consumers from joining together in collective lawsuits, shielding companies from aggregate accountability for widespread small-dollar overcharges.

rules.explanation: Forces every consumer into isolated individual dispute proceedings, preventing class-wide relief for systematic issues.
rules.recommendation: Understand that you cannot join a class settlement if the company engages in unauthorized billing.

rules.title: 30-Day Written Mail Opt-Out Provision

statute.title: Dispute Resolution Opt-Out Mechanism
statute.plainExplanation: A provision allowing consumers to reject binding arbitration and preserve court access if notice is provided within a limited timeframe.

rules.explanation: You have a legally protected window to preserve your court rights by sending written notice.
rules.recommendation: Exercise this right immediately upon opening your account if you wish to retain courtroom protections.

rules.title: Unilateral Contract Modification Without Prior Notice

statute.code: Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 211 / Illusory Promise Doctrine
statute.title: Common Law Contract Modification Standards
statute.plainExplanation: While common in commercial terms, courts scrutinize clauses granting unlimited unilateral rights to alter material terms without advance notice or opt-out rights as potentially unenforceable illusory promises.

rules.explanation: The platform claims the power to rewrite their agreement with you at any time without advance notice or affirmative re-consent.
rules.recommendation: Periodically monitor recurring pricing and terms directly rather than assuming terms remain fixed.

rules.title: Passive Deemed Consent via Continued Usage

statute.title: Inferred Consent & Unfair Trade Practice
statute.plainExplanation: Treating silence or normal app usage as affirmative assent to modified material terms is scrutinized as an unfair business practice.

rules.explanation: Simply logging into your account is treated by the company as your legal signature accepting their newly revised terms.
rules.recommendation: Check policy revision dates if you notice billing or feature changes in your service.
